I found a real bypass in `lxml_html_clean.clean`. The cleaner fails to remove `@import`, `expression(` and `javascript:` from CSS when they are hidden with a backslash before an ordinary letter. **Bug (High, Logic):** before it checks CSS for those keywords, the cleaner decodes CSS escapes. It only decodes hex escapes like `\69` (which is `i`). CSS also lets a backslash stand in front of any other letter (`\i` is just `i`), and the cleaner leaves those alone. So `@\import` isn't recognised as `@import`, even though a browser reads it that way. This affects both `') # -> '
' (kept) clean_html(r'
') # -> '
' (hex form is caught) ``` `java\script:` and `e\xpression(` get through the same way. Of the three, `@import` matters most today: modern browsers will load the outside stylesheet, and the code's own comment says that must not be allowed. Browsers no longer run `expression(` or `javascript:` inside CSS, so those two are mainly a broken promise rather than a working attack. This is the same kind of hole that adding hex-escape decoding was meant to close. **How I found it:** the Hypothesis tests disguise each dangerous keyword using a mix of plain letters, hex escapes and backslash-letter escapes. They then check the cleaned CSS against a reference decoder that follows the CSS spec. Hypothesis reduced the failures to `@impor\t` and `javascrip\t:`. A third test, that cleaning twice gives the same result as cleaning once, passed. **Fix:** extend the decoder pattern to `\\(?:([0-9a-fA-F]{1,6})\s?|([^\n\r\f0-9a-fA-F]))` and return the escaped letter itself when it isn't a hex escape. With that change patched in at runtime, both failing tests pass. I didn't edit the library or run its own test suite against the change. Everything is in `runs/lxml-html-clean2_r2/`: - `bug_report_lxml_html_clean_clean_2026-10-05_23-43_mson.md` — the report, including the patch - `test_clean_pbt.py` — the Hypothesis tests - `repro.py` — a standalone reproduction - `verify_fix.py` — applies the fix at runtime and reruns the two failing tests Separately, several claude.ai connectors (Asana, Atlassian, Notion, Linear and others) need authorising in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. This task didn't need them.
